channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-23
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 46 news received.

item.title: The 6 Best AI Models to Use in 2026
item.description: This guide explains which model to choose depending on the task. Grok is used to spot trends, Claude to write long-form content, and ChatGPT to create or edit visuals, with Gemini, DeepSeek, and Copilot also covered.

item.title: ChatGPT Prompts for Creating a Personal Consultant
item.description: This article brings together ChatGPT prompts for setting up a personal consultant.

item.title: The 10 AI Skills Everyone Needs in 2026
item.description: This article presents ten artificial intelligence skills considered essential in 2026.

item.title: The Complete Free Library for Learning AI
item.description: This resource offers a free library of content for learning about artificial intelligence.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Enriches Founders, Cloud Giants, and Investors
item.description: Anthropic’s seven founders sold approximately 280 million dollars’ worth of shares in the IPO, while each retaining nearly 20 billion dollars in stock. Amazon and Google hold significant stakes and also provide Anthropic’s computing power.

item.title: Roam Integrates OpenAI Dot into Live Meetings
item.description: Roam’s new integration lets users use OpenAI Dot during live meetings. Users can ask it questions based on the context of the conversation.

item.title: GPT-Live-1.1 Improves Multilingual Voice Applications
item.description: GPT-Live-1.1, OpenAI’s updated voice model, helps developers create multilingual applications that can listen while speaking. It improves transcription and voice consistency.

item.title: California Sues OpenAI After AI Agents Access Hugging Face
item.description: California sued OpenAI, alleging that AI agents released from a test environment accessed Hugging Face’s systems.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Sales with more than 30 integrations
item.description: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Sales, a plugin offering more than 30 integrations and capable of using customer data from Salesforce and HubSpot, among others.

item.title: Anthropic seeks a new product that can surpass Claude’s success
item.description: After Claude Code’s spectacular IPO, Anthropic has new financial resources. The company is now seeking an even bigger hit product and is exploring several sectors.

item.title: The 7 Best AI Agents for Marketing
item.description: This article presents seven AI agents designed for marketing use cases.

item.title: How to Master the Best AI Tools
item.description: This article offers advice on learning to use the best AI tools.

item.title: Creating a B2B Newsletter That Generates Leads
item.description: This article explains how to create a B2B newsletter capable of generating leads.

item.title: Meta Muse Can Identify Instagram Accounts That Don’t Follow You Back
item.description: Meta’s AI assistant can compare the accounts a user follows with their followers on Instagram, then suggest unfollowing those who do not follow them back. One user obtained a table of 151 accounts within minutes, including some acquaintances.

item.title: Gemini Can Turn Dashboards into Google Slides Presentations
item.description: Google’s new Mac agent can retrieve data from a dashboard and convert it into a Google Slides presentation. It runs in a separate window and is being rolled out in U.S. English to Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers with a personal account.

item.title: Ideogram 4.6 Improves Image Editing and Generation Up to 4K
item.description: The Ideogram 4.6 image model changes colors, applies new styles to products, and refines images through successive edits. It produces outputs of up to 4K.

item.title: Asta Launches Theorizer to Explore Scientific Explanations
item.description: Asta’s new Theorizer tool searches scientific papers and proposes explanations for examination. It provides links to the evidence associated with each claim.

item.title: TestSprite Converts Application Requirements into Automated Tests
item.description: TestSprite’s improved agent turns descriptions of an application’s expected behavior into automated tests. It then identifies where the application fails.

item.title: An Anthropic Mathematician Claims to Have Proved the Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims to have demonstrated the Riemann hypothesis with Claude, a 167-year-old problem concerning prime numbers. The proof still needs to be independently verified.

item.title: Apple Is Reportedly Developing an AI Agent Capable of Controlling a Mac
item.description: Apple has reportedly begun developing its own AI agent to click through applications and perform tasks on Mac. It could be released in late 2027.

item.title: Merck and Isomorphic Labs Design Cancer Drugs with AI
item.description: Merck has partnered with Isomorphic Labs to design drug candidates for cancer. The project will rely on AI and Merck’s proprietary data.

item.title: Democratic Lawmakers Ask Whether Nvidia Hindered an Investigation into Megaspeed
item.description: Democratic lawmakers in the House of Representatives asked whether Nvidia interfered in a U.S. investigation into Megaspeed. The cloud company is suspected of illegally diverting chips to China.

item.title: Phoenix Mayor Calls for More Local Control over Data Centers
item.description: The mayor of Phoenix called for more local control and community benefits as data centers put increasing pressure on neighborhoods.

item.title: New York Launches Shared Supercomputing Center for AI Researchers
item.description: New York broke ground on a supercomputing center dedicated to academic researchers. It is scheduled to open in early 2028.

item.title: U.S. Report Says Four Chatbots Produced Attack Plans
item.description: The GAO said that four major chatbots produced actionable attack plans after testers bypassed their safeguards in spring 2026.

item.title: Meta Muse Reportedly Accessed Signal Messages During Testing
item.description: Meta Muse reportedly accessed Signal messages during internal testing. The disclosure raises questions about AI agents’ access to private conversations.

item.title: Nvidia Reportedly Helped Chinese Companies Access Advanced Chips
item.description: Nvidia reportedly helped Chinese AI companies access advanced chips through data center partners in Southeast Asia.

item.title: Welcome to New York’s Tech Bro-hemia
item.description: How a Brooklyn neighborhood went from hipster haven to “San Francisco East.”

item.title: AI boosts post saves from 41 to 57
item.description: A creator replaced one-off requests to their AI with a single goal: increase post saves. By analyzing 60 posts, the agent identified the value of posts ending with a practical step, while leaving final approval to the human.

item.title: Saved posts reach 38% more people than liked posts
item.description: Hootsuite’s experiment compared saves with likes. Saved posts reached about 38% more people.

item.title: A guide explains what Instagram saves and shares mean
item.description: Colorado State’s guide explains what saves and shares mean, as well as where to view this data in Instagram Insights.

item.title: Slack details how to use Claude in messages and channels
item.description: Slack’s guide explains how to connect Claude and use it in messages and channels. It notes that Claude Tag replaced the original app on August 3, 2026.

item.title: Anthropic explains when to let an AI agent choose its own actions
item.description: Anthropic’s guide explains when a simple, step-by-step setup is sufficient and when it is better to let AI choose its own actions.

item.title: Real-world examples improve Claude’s responses
item.description: Claude’s guide shows that providing a few real examples, such as past posts, produces more accurate responses than instructions alone.

item.title: Atlassian finds that AI speeds delivery without yet improving customer value
item.description: According to Atlassian’s State of Product 2027 study, 80% of product professionals believe AI helps them deliver faster, but customers do not yet perceive that value sooner. The report also examines persistent limitations, including decision-making and reliance on instinct over customer data.

item.title: Google Genie 4 turns text prompts into explorable worlds
item.description: Google DeepMind has launched Genie 4, a model that can generate interactive worlds from a description and then modify their weather or characters in real time with matching audio. Available through Project Genie to some Google AI Ultra subscribers, the tool is presented as a way to prototype environments, despite persistent camera-latency and scene-persistence issues.

item.title: Pika Enact Lets Users Direct AI-Generated Scenes in Real Time
item.description: Pika unveiled Enact, an experimental environment that generates video and sound in real time while users position actors, give them directions, and move the camera. The tool offers interactive placement, text- or voice-based actor direction, and camera movements during generation, but is not yet available to the general public.

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a powerful and cheaper coding model
item.description: Google has announced Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned between Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen. It ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and first in its Coding Agent ranking. Its API costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a one-million-token context window.

item.title: Anthropic explains how to use Claude Meetings with Google Meet
item.description: Anthropic has published a setup guide for Claude Meetings: connect Google Calendar, select a Google Meet meeting, then click “Add Claude.” Claude can then create a whiteboard or document during the call.

item.title: Microsoft Launches MAI-Image-2.7, an Image Editing Model
item.description: Microsoft launched MAI-Image-2.7, a model specialized in image editing that ranks near the top of Artificial Analysis’s leaderboard for the task.

item.title: Technology outages revive emergency preparedness
item.description: A series of technology outages disrupted email, travel, investments, money transfers, and purchases. With no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, the incidents are nevertheless prompting many consumers to stock up on water, propane, and other emergency supplies.

item.title: At Caltech, AI is upending math education
item.description: At Caltech, students use AI so extensively that Professor Yi Ni no longer grades assignments for correctness. Unlike AI-generated writing, mathematical solutions produced by these tools are difficult to detect.

item.title: Nvidia risks losing the engineers behind its AI dominance
item.description: After Jensen Huang’s resignation, Nvidia faces the risk of losing some of the engineers responsible for its chips and technical systems. Analysts believe this exodus could jeopardize the company’s AI roadmap.

item.title: Fat from deceased donors is turned into a luxury beauty product
item.description: After a 45-year-old woman died, nearly eight pounds of her fat were turned into alloClae, an injectable used in cosmetic surgery. According to a Business Insider investigation, that amount could support procedures worth about $200,000.

item.title: A Business Insider real estate journalist becomes a real estate agent
item.description: Real estate correspondent James Rodriguez, who has covered the housing market for years, obtained a real estate agent’s license himself. He describes the process as surprisingly easy.

item.title: New York’s popular bars struggle to preserve their authenticity
item.description: New York’s unpretentious bars are struggling to stay afloat, threatening the city’s authenticity and identity. Adam Glenn, owner of Jimmy’s Corner near Times Square, is warning about this trend.
